entries.topic: Quenched lattice glueball spectrum - Morningstar-Peardon 1999 (digest ref [2])
entries.content: C. J. Morningstar & M. J. Peardon, 'The glueball spectrum from an anisotropic lattice study', Phys. Rev. D 60, 034509 (1999), arXiv:hep-lat/9901004. SU(3) pure-gauge (quenched), Monte Carlo on several anisotropic lattices with spatial spacings 0.1-0.4 fm; ~13 glueballs identified below 4 GeV; scale set by hadronic scale r0 (not string tension). Masses: 0++ = 1730(50)(80) MeV (often quoted 1730+-80 or 1730(90)); 2++ = 2400(25)(120) MeV (2400+-120); 0-+ = 2590(40)(130) MeV (2590+-130). These are THE standard quenched reference values. Matches the digest's claim that X(2370) sits inside the LQCD 0-+ window.

entries.topic: Quenched lattice glueball spectrum - Chen et al 2006 (digest ref [3])
entries.content: Y. Chen et al., 'Glueball spectrum and matrix elements on anisotropic lattices', Phys. Rev. D 73, 014516 (2006), arXiv:hep-lat/0510074. Quenched anisotropic lattices, spatial spacing 0.1-0.2 fm; also computes glueball-to-vacuum matrix elements of local gluonic operators in scalar/tensor/pseudoscalar channels. Masses: 0++ = 1710(50)(80) MeV, 2++ = 2390(30)(120) MeV, 0-+ = 2560(35)(120) MeV. Fully consistent with Morningstar-Peardon; also uses r0 for scale (Meyer-Teper instead used string tension).

entries.topic: RATIO 0-+/0++ (computed from snippet-verified central values)
entries.content: Morningstar-Peardon: 2590/1730 = 1.497. Chen et al 2006: 2560/1710 = 1.497. The quenched ratio m(0-+)/m(0++) ~= 1.50 is remarkably stable across the two standard studies (my arithmetic on snippet-verified central values). Using instead Gui et al 2019's 0-+ = 2.395 GeV against 0++ = 1.71-1.73 GeV gives ratio ~= 1.39-1.40, showing a genuine ~4-8% spread in the quenched 0-+ mass (2.4-2.6 GeV) across scale-setting/extrapolation choices. In sigma units with sqrt(sigma)=440 MeV: m(0-+)/sqrt(sigma) = 5.8-5.9 (MP99/Chen06) or 5.4 (Gui19); X(2370) at combined mass 2359 MeV has m/sqrt(sigma) = 5.36 at sigma=0.194 GeV^2 - i.e. the BESIII state sits at the LOW edge of the quenched band, closest to the Gui et al 2019 value.

entries.topic: Gui et al 2019 pseudoscalar glueball + J/psi radiative production (digest ref [5])
entries.content: L.-C. Gui, J.-M. Dong, Y. Chen, Y.-B. Yang, 'Study of the pseudoscalar glueball in J/psi radiative decays', Phys. Rev. D 100, 054511 (2019), arXiv:1906.03666. Quenched approximation, three anisotropic lattices with a_s = 0.222(2) to 0.110(1) fm, continuum-extrapolated. Pseudoscalar glueball mass m(G 0-+) = 2.395(14) GeV (digest's '2.395 GeV' EXACT). entries.content: (a) Gregory, Irving, Lucini, McNeile, Rago, Richards, Rinaldi, 'Towards the glueball spectrum from unquenched lattice QCD', JHEP 10 (2012) 170, arXiv:1208.1858: Nf=2+1 ASQTAD improved staggered fermions, 2150 configurations, a = 0.092 fm, m_pi = 360 MeV, variational technique, 10 glueball states; scalar glueball 1795(60) MeV; overall conclusion that unquenching effects on glueball masses appear small. C 42, 093103 (2018), arXiv:1702.08174: clover Wilson, heavy pions (m_pi ~ 938 and 650 MeV); tensor ground state ~2.4 GeV and pseudoscalar (gluonic operators) ~2.6 GeV, both compatible with quenched values. entries.topic: Isgur-Paton flux-tube (closed-loop) glueball model
entries.content: N. Isgur & J. Paton, 'Flux-tube model for hadrons in QCD', Phys. Rev. D 31, 2910 (1985). Glueballs modeled as CLOSED loops of fundamental chromoelectric flux ('rings of glue') with NO constituent gluons - closed bosonic string states. Quantization: transverse phonons on a loop of radius rho, frequency m/rho for mode m, each phonon carrying angular momentum +-m about the loop axis (clockwise/anticlockwise circulation); each phonon configuration additionally carries an infinite tower of radial (breathing) excitations; adiabatic separation + small-oscillation approximation. LOWEST STATE: J^PC = 0++ at 1.52 GeV (snippet-confirmed). Distinctive feature: low-lying odd-spin PC = +- ('oddball') states appear in the closed-tube spectrum. Phononic Regge behavior at large spin: J ~ M^2/(8 pi sigma), i.e. a slope 1/4 of the open-string (meson) slope 1/(2 pi sigma) for the phonon mode (orbital mode differs). The digest's GUM analog (closed knot-free Z3 mismatch-tube loop, mass set by sigma) is exactly this model class - snippet-confirmed that this is a recognized, lattice-benchmarked framework.

entries.topic: Johnson-Teper extended Isgur-Paton model vs lattice
entries.content: R. W. Johnson & M. Teper: (a) 'An extended Isgur-Paton model: agreement with the lattice?', hep-lat/9709083, Nucl. Phys. Proc. Suppl. 63 (1998) 197-199; (b) 'String models of glueballs and the spectrum of SU(N) gauge theories in 2+1 dimensions', Phys. Rev. D 66, 036006 (2002). Extensions: string curvature/rigidity term, improved short-distance cutoff, and (in D=2+1) mixing via higher topological contributions. RESULT: in D=2+1 the extended model agrees reasonably with lattice SU(N) spectra and is 'remarkably successful' for C=+ states; in D=3+1 a QUALITATIVE discrepancy remains - the model predicts a low-lying 1-+ (orbital excitation of the 0++ ground loop) whereas the lattice 1-+ is heavy. Earlier SU(2) comparison in D=3,4: hep-lat/9312035. Direct campaign relevance: any GUM closed-loop spectrum must confront the same 1-+ orbital-excitation problem.

entries.topic: Modern closed-flux-tube (torelon) spectra and Nambu-Goto closed-string formula
entries.content: Athenodorou, Bringoltz & Teper, 'Closed flux tubes and their string description in D=3+1 SU(N) gauge theories', JHEP (2011), arXiv:1007.4720 (SU(3),SU(5),SU(6), two lattice spacings; states labeled by spin J, transverse/longitudinal parities, longitudinal momentum p): most low-lying closed-flux-tube states are well described by the FREE Nambu-Goto string spectrum, remarkably even at short lengths where excitation energies >> sqrt(sigma); EXCEPTION: some J^P = 0- states deviate strongly from Nambu-Goto in D=3+1 - later identified as a massive pseudoscalar excitation on the worldsheet, the 'worldsheet axion' (Athenodorou-Dubovsky-Luo-Teper, arXiv:2112.11213; 'Eight very excited flux tube spectra...', PRD 107, 114507 (2023)). Nambu-Goto closed-string (winding l, momentum q) energy levels: E^2_{NL,NR}(q,l) = (sigma l)^2 + 8 pi sigma [ (NL+NR)/2 - (D-2)/24 ] + (2 pi q / l)^2, with level matching NL - NR = q. D=2+1 analogs: arXiv:0709.0693, 0809.4431, 1103.5854. Campaign hook: the 0- anomaly is the parity-structure modifier slot the digest flags for GUM chirality.

entries.topic: Closed-string glueball Regge slope / m vs sqrt(sigma) relations
entries.content: (a) Sonnenschein & Weissman, 'Glueballs as rotating folded closed strings', JHEP 12 (2015) 011, arXiv:1507.01604: closed-string (glueball) Regge trajectories have HALF the open-string slope - alpha'_closed ~= 0.45 GeV^-2 vs meson alpha' ~= 0.9 GeV^-2, i.e. J = alpha'/2 M^2 + intercept; they advocate searching flavorless resonances at 2.4-3 GeV on such trajectories. (b) Dubovsky & Hernandez-Chifflet, 'Yang-Mills glueballs as closed bosonic strings', arXiv:1611.09796 (JHEP 2017): Axionic String Ansatz - glueballs are quantized closed-string states; in 3D no extra worldsheet dof, fixing J^PC of ~39 lattice glueball states with good agreement; in 4D the glueball spectrum requires the massive pseudoscalar worldsheet mode (axion). Also '3D Yang-Mills glueballs vs closed effective strings' arXiv:2104.02154. (c) Combined with entry above, the closed-string program gives concrete m^2-vs-sigma templates: leading closed-string mass scale m^2 ~ 8 pi sigma (N - (D-2)/24)-type (contracted loop limit) and slope-1/(4 pi sigma)-class trajectories; lattice anchor m(0++)/sqrt(sigma) ~= 3.5 (Lucini-Teper SU(3)/large-N continuum).

entries.topic: Glueball-ccbar mixing: Zhang et al PLB 827, 136960 (2022) (digest ref [10])
entries.content: R. Zhang, W. Sun, Y. Chen, M. Gong, L.-C. Gui (+ others), 'The glueball content of eta_c', Phys. Lett. B 827, 136960 (2022), arXiv:2107.12749. FIRST lattice-QCD derivation of the mixing energy and mixing angle of pseudoscalar charmonium and the pseudoscalar glueball; two gauge ensembles with Nf=2 degenerate dynamical CHARM quarks; mixing energy 49(6) MeV on the near-physical-charm ensemble, insensitive to charm-quark mass; a mixing angle theta = 4.6(6) degrees appears in the search results for this study - consistent with the digest's '2-5 degrees' band (attribution of the exact 4.6(6) number to this paper flagged in unverified). Light-quark counterpart: 'eta-glueball mixing from Nf=2 lattice QCD', PRD 107, 094510 (2023), arXiv:2205.12541.

entries.topic: Chen-Gui-Li-Sun 2026 production-rate enhancement via mixing (digest ref [11])
entries.content: Y. Chen, L.-C. Gui, G. Li, W. Sun, 'Production Rate of Glueball-like X(2370) in J/psi Radiative Decay', arXiv:2605.01757 (2026). Mechanism snippet-confirmed: X(2370) and eta_c treated as admixtures of G(0-+) and ccbar(0-) with small mixing angle sin(theta) (citing the PLB 827 lattice mixing); Br[J/psi -> gamma eta_c] is INSENSITIVE to small theta, but Br[J/psi -> gamma X(2370)] is enlarged DRASTICALLY because the J/psi -> gamma ccbar(0-) transition has a much larger form factor and the gamma X(2370) mode a much larger kinematic (phase-space) factor; result can far exceed the pure-glueball 2.3(8)x10^-4. Snippets state 'present results by BESIII favor a small mixing angle of O(1 degree)'. The digest's exact printed band '2-5 degrees -> (2-20)x10^-3' could NOT be pinned from snippets (listed in unverified). KEY STRUCTURAL POINT confirmed: in this picture the 0-+ glueball is only observable as the glueball-dominant member of a G-ccbar mixture.

entries.topic: sqrt-OZI rule (Robson 1977, digest ref [16])
entries.content: D. Robson, 'A basic guide for the glueball spotter', Nucl. Phys. B 130, 328-348 (1977) - reference details snippet-confirmed. Modern statement (as used by BESIII 2607.20366 and reviews): glueball decays to qqbar are OZI-suppressed at only ONE vertex, because a glueball has no initial qqbar pair to annihilate (ordinary OZI-forbidden meson decays are suppressed at two vertices); hence the glueball partial width is approximately the GEOMETRIC MEAN sqrt(Gamma_OZI-allowed x Gamma_doubly-OZI-suppressed) - the 'sqrt-OZI rule'. Snippets also note the rule implies suppression factors of ~3-10 per channel, giving few-MeV partial widths per exclusive mode, matching the digest's criterion 6 logic. Whether the sqrt formula appears verbatim in Robson's 1977 text could not be checked (paper not accessible) - flagged unverified.

entries.topic: Scalar glueball candidates f0(1710)/f0(1500) status + scalar radiative production
entries.content: Candidates near the quenched 0++ mass: f0(1370), f0(1500), f0(1710). Historical favorite was f0(1500); the modern balance has shifted to f0(1710) as glueball-DOMINANT: (a) lattice: Gui et al (CLQCD), 'Scalar glueball in radiative J/psi decay on the lattice', PRL 110, 021601 (2013), arXiv:1206.0125 - partial width J/psi -> gamma G(0++) = 0.35(8) keV, i.e. Br = 3.8(9)x10^-3 (NOTE: 10^-3, cross-checked by arithmetic 0.35 keV / 92.9 keV ~= 3.8x10^-3; updated by 'The radiative decay of scalar glueball from lattice QCD', arXiv:2404.01564, Sci. China PMA 2024); this large predicted rate is compatible with the measured f0(1710) production and about an order of magnitude above f0(1500)'s. (b) Phenomenology (extended linear sigma model, coupled-channel reviews): f0(1710) mostly gluonic, f0(1500) close to an SU(3) octet; but the assignment is still not settled at PDG level - competing analyses keep significant glueball fractions spread over f0(1710)/f0(1770)/f0(2100). (c) The 2++ analog 'Is f2(2340) the tensor glueball?' discussions exist (PRD 108, 014023). Net: 0++ candidate situation remains mixed/unresolved, in contrast to the cleaner 0-+ X(2370) case.

entries.topic: 'Lattice evidence that scalar glueballs are small' (arXiv:2508.21821) - FOUND
entries.content: R. Abbott, D. C. Hackett, D. A. Pefkou, F. Romero-Lopez, P. E. Shanahan (MIT CTP group), 'Lattice evidence that scalar glueballs are small', arXiv:2508.21821, published in Phys. Rev. Lett. (new-style DOI 10.1103/67xg-qxhz; OSTI record 3016205). First calculation of the gravitational form factors (GFFs) of the scalar glueball, in pure Yang-Mills theory at a single lattice spacing. Headline number: scalar glueball MASS RADIUS = 0.263(31) fm - significantly smaller than other hadrons (supports earlier suggestions of a compact glueball); GFF comparison indicates glueballs have a gluonic structure different from typical hadrons; authors propose smallness as a smoking-gun target for experimental glueball searches. Campaign relevance: a small (sub-0.3 fm) 0++ glueball constrains the size of any GUM closed-loop realization.

entries.topic: String tension sigma ~ 0.18-0.19 GeV^2 provenance
entries.content: Two independent roots, both snippet-confirmed: (1) REGGE: meson/baryon Regge slope alpha' ~= 0.9 GeV^-2 (e.g. alpha' = 0.909 GeV^-2); rotating-string relation sigma = 1/(2 pi alpha') gives sigma ~= 0.175-0.18 GeV^2, sqrt(sigma) ~= 420-430 MeV (sqrt(0.9-slope value) -> 421 MeV; alpha'=0.84 GeV^-2 corresponds to sqrt(sigma)=430 MeV). (2) LATTICE/potential models: accepted value sqrt(sigma) ~= 440 MeV (range 420-440), i.e. sigma ~= 0.176-0.194 GeV^2, used for quenched scale setting (Teper, Lucini-Teper; MP99/Chen06 instead set scale by r0). Continuum anchor ratio: m(0++)/sqrt(sigma) ~= 3.5 in SU(3)/large-N. So the GUM corpus value sigma = 0.19 GeV^2 (sqrt(sigma) ~= 436 MeV) is exactly the standard lattice convention, at the top of the Regge-derived range.

entries.topic: Chain 3 — 2024 spin-parity (PRL 132, 181901)
entries.content: 'Determination of Spin-Parity Quantum Numbers of X(2370) as 0-+ from J/psi -> gamma KS0 KS0 eta'' — first PWA, (10087±44)e6 J/psi. X(2370) significance >11.7 sigma; JPC = 0-+ determined for the first time; 0-+ preferred over 1++ at >10.8 sigma and over 2-+ at >9.8 sigma (this reconciles the digest's '>9.8 sigma' — it is the weakest-alternative discrimination floor, not the state significance). M = 2395 ± 11(stat) +26/-94(syst) MeV/c2; Gamma = 188 +18/-17(stat) +124/-33(syst) MeV; B[J/psi->gammaX]·B[X->f0(980)eta']·B[f0->KSKS] = (1.31±0.22 +2.85/-0.84)e-5. Stated consistent with lightest pseudoscalar glueball predictions. arXiv:2312.05324. Selected into the PRL 2024 most-important-papers collection (IHEP notice, Apr 2025). IHEP issued a 2024 EurekAlert release 'BESIII collaboration discovers glueball-like particle—X(2370)' (release 1045244).

entries.topic: Chain 4 — 2026 new modes + combined 2359/170 (arXiv:2605.26495)
entries.content: Title confirmed: 'Observation of the X(2370) in J/psi -> gamma KS0 KS0 pi0 and J/psi -> gamma pi0 pi0 eta'. New decay modes KS0KS0pi0 (>14 sigma) and pi0pi0eta (>20 sigma); X(2370) -> a0(980)0 pi0, a0 -> pi0 eta observed at >9 sigma (first quasi-two-body mode fully containing the isovector channel). Combining measurements across decay channels: M = 2359 +13/-14 MeV/c2, Gamma = 170 +44/-29 MeV — these are exactly the values the 2607.20366 Letter fixes in its K*Kbar fit (digest ref 28). Central values 2359/170 dual-anchored (digest + web snippet); uncertainties snippet-level only.

entries.topic: Chain 5 — 2026 flavor-singlet Letter (arXiv:2607.20366, submitted 22 Jul 2026)
entries.content: 'Lightest 0-+ Glueball as Dominant Constituent of X(2370)', BESIII, 10.087e9 J/psi: search for X(2370) -> K*(892)0 Kbar0 via gamma KS0KS0pi0; no peak (0.1 sigma); B[J/psi->gammaX]·B[X->K*Kbar->KSKSpi0] < 2.7e-6 at 90% CL; ratio to KSKSpi0 R < 0.081 at 90% CL; K*(892)Kbar forbidden for a 0-+ flavor singlet by generalized G-parity (Lipkin PLB 106,114; PLB 109,326; Klempt-Zaitsev Phys.Rept.454,1) => first flavor-singlet light hadron above 1 GeV; implied partial width to K*Kbar < 2 MeV vs 15-200 MeV expected for an eta/eta' radial excitation. Web snippets confirm title, date, 2.7e-6 limit, flavor-singlet claim, and the disfavoring of Sigma-Sigmabar baryonium (no line-shape distortion at the SigmaSigmabar threshold, production rate too high for baryonium, baryonium not flavor-singlet). Digest is a direct read of the full PDF.

entries.topic: Chain 6 — ICHEP 2026 announcement + press cycle
entries.content: Presented Aug 5, 2026 in a special plenary at ICHEP 2026 (43rd ICHEP, July 30–Aug 5, Natal Convention Center, Natal, Brazil); CERN Indico contribution titled 'Lightest 0-+ glueball as dominant constituent of X(2370)' (event 1522800, contribution 7201543). IHEP English press release 'BESIII Experiment Identifies X(2370) as a Glueball-dominated Particle' dated ~Aug 13, 2026; EurekAlert release 1139079; phys.org 'X(2370) emerges as glueball-dominated particle in collider experiments' (Aug 2026); Xinhua Aug 6, 2026; Science/AAAS 'Behold the glueball, a strange new form of matter' (~Aug 8–12, Slashdot pickup Aug 12); Nature news 'A particle made of force: physicists say they have found mysterious glueball' (d41586-026-02498-1) + Nature daily briefing (d41586-026-02558-6). Framing throughout: 'complete experimental evidence chain' spanning mass, quantum numbers, production, decay pattern, flavor; official wording is 'dominant constituent ... is a pseudoscalar glueball' — explicitly NOT 'pure glueball'.

entries.topic: Skepticism/caveats — 2026 community reaction quotes
entries.content: Nature news: Bruce Yabsley (particle physicist): 'There is no single smoking gun that proves that this particle is made of glueballs', though findings are 'quite persuasive'; also the evidence is not enough to rule out X(2370) being made of other types of particle. Science/AAAS: Colin Morningstar (CMU, lattice QCD): 'This is probably as close as we are going to get' (supportive — three main expected glueball properties matched); William Detmold (MIT): a completely quark-free particle is impossible — a small quark component is always present through mixing, i.e. the identification is intrinsically 'dominant component', never 'pure'. Press-level caveats (XenoSpectrum, techtimes): the gluonic mixing fraction has NOT been quantitatively established; higher-statistics studies of additional channels needed; independent confirmation from another experiment (no other facility currently has a comparable J/psi sample — BESIII is effectively the only source) still required before 'undisputed discovery'; scalar (0++) and tensor glueball sectors remain unsettled.

entries.topic: Skepticism — published anti-glueball analysis: 'Nature of X(2370)' (PRD 105, 034010, 2022)
entries.content: Xiang Sun, Ling-Yun Dai, Shi-Qing Kuang, Wen Qin, A.P. Szczepaniak (arXiv:2110.08827): dispersive/effective-chiral-Lagrangian analysis of J/psi -> gamma(K+K-eta', KSKSeta', pi+pi-eta'); found decays into three pseudoscalars well described, but the EXTRACTED B[J/psi->gammaX(2370)] is an order of magnitude LARGER than the LQCD pure-glueball production rate ((2.31±0.90)e-4, Gui et al 2019) => concluded X(2370) 'not likely a glueball'. The 2026 Letter counter-argues: (i) glueball–ccbar(0-+) mixing with a tiny angle raises the expected rate to 1e-3-scale (refs 10,11), and (ii) this paper's own solution implied B(KKbarpi)/B(KKbareta') > 50, inconsistent with the measured ratio ~8.3 (Letter Table I). NOTE the historical inversion: the same high production rate was evidence AGAINST a pure glueball in 2022 and is evidence FOR a mixed glueball-dominant state in 2026 — the mixing mechanism is the load-bearing new ingredient.

entries.topic: Production-mixing keystone paper (arXiv:2605.01757, May 2026)
entries.content: Ying Chen, Long-Cheng Gui, Geng Li, Wei Sun, 'Production Rate of Glueball-like X(2370) in J/psi Radiative Decay': lattice-QCD-motivated mixing of the pseudoscalar glueball G(0-) with the lowest ccbar(0-) (mixing predicted in Zhang et al., PLB 827, 136960 (2022)); B[J/psi->gamma eta_c] is insensitive to small sin(theta) but B[J/psi->gammaX(2370)] is drastically enlarged (much larger kinematic factor and ccbar transition form factor). Abstract snippet: 'present results by BESIII favor a small mixing angle of order 1 degree'. DISCREPANCY FLAG: the digest (from the Letter PDF) prints '2–5 degrees raises it to (2–20)e-3' attributed to this ref — the abstract's 'order 1 degree' vs the Letter's '2–5 degrees' should be checked against both full texts when egress allows. Structural corollary printed in the Letter: via this mechanism the 0-+ glueball can only ever appear as the glueball-dominant member of a glueball–ccbar admixture.
entries.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01757 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.01757 ; local digest Sec.4 item 3

entries.topic: Alternative 1 — eta/eta' radial excitation (CITATION CORRECTION: PRD 83, 114007, not 114021)
entries.content: Jie-Sheng Yu, Zhi-Feng Sun, Xiang Liu, Qiang Zhao, 'Categorizing resonances X(1835), X(2120), and X(2370) in the pseudoscalar meson family', Phys. Rev. D 83, 114007 (2011), arXiv:1104.3064: X(1835) = second radial excitation of eta'(958); X(2120) and X(2370) explainable as third and fourth radial excitations of eta(548)/eta'(958). IMPORTANT: 'PRD 83, 114021' (as printed in the digest and the tasking) is a DIFFERENT paper (B. Gong, J.-X. Wang, H.-F. Zhang, J/psi hadroproduction at NLO) — the correct article number is 114007; the campaign digest (and possibly the Letter's ref [22] as transcribed) should be corrected. Status post-2026: the radial-excitation assignment is the alternative most directly killed by the K*Kbar null — such states are expected to decay to K*(892)Kbar with 10s-of-MeV partial width (the eta(1405)/eta(1475) analogs do), vs <2 MeV measured.

entries.topic: Alternative 1b — the 15–200 MeV K*Kbar width source (PRD 96, 034013)
entries.content: L.-M. Wang, S.-Q. Luo, Z.-F. Sun, X. Liu, 'Constructing new pseudoscalar meson nonets with the observed X(2100), X(2500), and eta(2225)', Phys. Rev. D 96, 034013 (2017), arXiv:1705.00549 — title/authors/number multiply corroborated. This is the Letter's ref [38], which together with PRD 83 114007 underlies the quoted 15–200 MeV expected Gamma(X->K*(892)Kbar) for an eta/eta' radial excitation at 2.37 GeV; the Letter adds a naive eta(1405)/eta(1475) extrapolation (>10 MeV) times a ~30x larger P-wave phase space => >20 MeV, vs measured <2 MeV. The 15–200 MeV range itself is printed in the Letter (digest Sec.5); I could not read the theory papers' tables to independently confirm the range endpoints — listed in unverified.

entries.topic: Alternative 2 — 4-quark interpretations and current status
entries.content: (a) N. Su, H.-X. Chen, 'S- and P-wave fully-strange tetraquark states from QCD sum rules', PRD 106, 014023 (2022), arXiv:2204.13959: X(2370) as a P-wave ss-sbar-sbar (ss̄s̄s) tetraquark with JPC = 0-+. (b) R.-R. Dong, N. Su, H.-X. Chen, E.-L. Cui, Z.-Y. Zhou, Eur. Phys. J. C 80, 749 (2020): fully-strange tetraquark near 2.3 GeV (snippets partially conflate with X(2300) and give 1+- for some states; exact title/JPC assignment unverified — flagged). (c) Q.-N. Wang, D.-K. Lian, W. Chen, 'Interpreting the X(2370) and X(2600) as light tetraquark states', PRD 112, 034010 (published Aug 14, 2025), arXiv:2502.16047: QCD sum rules for ud-ubar-dbar, us-ubar-sbar, ss-sbar-sbar compact tetraquarks in 0-+ and 2-+ channels — a live post-spin-parity tetraquark assignment. (d) Ongoing 2026 work: 'Fully-strange tetraquarks: fall-apart decays and experimental candidates' (arXiv:2601.03614, Jan 2026) and chiral-quark-model studies (arXiv:2602.01759). Letter's counter (digest Sec.5): any light-quark-content multiquark should have OZI-allowed ~100 MeV partial widths (measured: few MeV per mode) and is not naturally flavor-singlet; gamma-omega/gamma-phi suppression bounds both u ubar+d dbar and s sbar content. An ss̄s̄s state specifically would need large K*Kbar/strangeness-rich couplings — in tension with the K*Kbar null, though a quantitative published post-Letter rebuttal by the tetraquark proponents was not found as of 2026-08-15.

entries.topic: Alternative 3 — baryonium
entries.content: Baryonium lineage: X(1835) as p-pbar bound state (Skyrme-model: hep-ph/0605303; Bethe-Salpeter analyses: arXiv:1006.2000, 1012.3325, 1105.0824 'Baryonium X(1835)'); within that program X(2370) was tentatively identified as a p̄N(1440)/pN(1400) bound state or Delta-Deltabar-dominant state ('Baryonia and near-threshold enhancements', arXiv:1306.6725). The 2026 Letter (digest Sec.5 + arXiv HTML snippet) disfavors the Sigma-Sigmabar (and general baryonium) option on three counts: J/psi radiative BFs to baryon pairs are ~1e-4 or smaller (vs >1e-3 needed for X(2370)), no line-shape distortion observed at the Sigma-Sigmabar threshold (m ~ 2·1193 = 2386 MeV, right at the mass), and baryonium is not a flavor singlet. Same interpretive family as the never-resolved X(1835)/X(ppbar) case.
entries.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.3325 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1306.6725 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.20366 ; local digest Sec.5

entries.topic: Contrast case — eta(1405)/eta(1475): the two-state/one-state puzzle
entries.content: PDG has listed TWO isoscalar pseudoscalars since the 2004 split of the historical E/iota(1440): eta(1405) decaying mainly a0(980)pi (+ isospin-violating f0(980)pi) and eta(1475) with K*(892)Kbar as its major mode. The iota(1440) was THE 1980s pseudoscalar-glueball candidate; that identification died because lattice QCD puts the 0-+ glueball at 2.3–2.6 GeV, and the state slots into the eta' radial-excitation family. Modern resolution trend: triangle-singularity (TS) mechanism — X.-G. Wu, J.-J. Wu, Q. Zhao, B.-S. Zou line ('Understanding the property of eta(1405/1475) in the J/psi radiative decay', arXiv:1211.2148; width effects arXiv:1905.04207; three-body unitary coupled-channel arXiv:2212.07904; KSKSpi0-spectrum reanalysis arXiv:2407.10234) — a SINGLE eta(~1440) whose apparent double peak and channel-dependent masses arise from K*Kbar loop rescattering; the TS also explains the anomalously large isospin-violating eta(1405)->f0(980)pi. Relevance as the Letter's foil: eta(1405)/eta(1475) decays copiously to K*(892)Kbar and has gamma-omega/gamma-phi products ~3.5e-6 (both), exactly the flavored/octet behavior X(2370) does NOT show — and it is a cautionary tale that J/psi-radiative pseudoscalar peaks can be lineshape artifacts, which is why the Letter's own caveat about interference/threshold effects (X(2120)/X(2260)/X(2600)) matters.
entries.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1211.2148 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.04207 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.07904 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.10234 ; local digest Secs.2,5

entries.topic: Prior candidate — X(1835): why it never resolved
entries.content: BES 2005: X(1835) in J/psi -> gamma eta' pi+ pi-, M ≈ 1833.7±6.2±2.7 MeV, Gamma ≈ 67.7±20.3±7.7 MeV; entangled with the 2003 J/psi -> gamma p pbar threshold enhancement X(ppbar) (JPC 0-+ from PWA). Competing interpretations never separated: p-pbar bound state/baryonium, eta' second radial excitation (Yu et al. PRD 83 114007), pseudoscalar glueball (arXiv:0801.4821 and others). BESIII 2016 (PRL 117, 042002; arXiv:1603.09653, 1.09e9 J/psi): anomalous line shape — abrupt slope change of the eta'pi+pi- spectrum exactly at the p-pbar threshold; BOTH a Flatte model (broad state strongly coupled to p-pbar) AND a coherent two-resonance model fit almost equally well (>7 sigma for either), so even the number of states is ambiguous. Reasons the glueball ID failed: mass ~1.84 GeV is far below the lattice 0-+ window (2.3–3.0 GeV); no flavor-singlet discriminant was ever measured; p-pbar threshold dynamics contaminate the lineshape; whether X(ppbar) and X(1835) are even the same state is unresolved. 'None of the hypotheses could be excluded' is the standing literature verdict — the anti-pattern the 2026 seven-criteria chain was designed to escape.

entries.topic: Prior candidates — f0(1500)/f0(1710) scalar-glueball saga: why unconfirmed for 30 years
entries.content: Quenched lattice puts the lightest glueball (0++) at ~1.45–1.75 GeV. Crystal Barrel's f0(1500) (LEAR, 1995) was claimed by Amsler–Close as scalar-glueball evidence (decay pattern incompatible with simple qqbar). But three isoscalar scalars — f0(1370), f0(1500), f0(1710) — overlap there, and all realistic descriptions are three-way qqbar(nnbar) + qqbar(ssbar) + G mixing schemes (Amsler–Close–Kirk; Close–Zhao hep-ph/0004241; He et al.; Cheng–Chua–Liu), which disagree on WHERE the glue sits: one school makes f0(1500) glue-rich; the opposing analysis makes f0(1710) glueball-dominant with f0(1500) glue content tiny (an SU(3) octet does not mix with G). Production data now lean f0(1710): quenched-lattice radiative width Gamma(J/psi->gamma G(0++)) = 0.35(8) keV => B ≈ 3.8(9)e-3 (Gui et al., PRL 110, 021601 (2013), arXiv:1206.0125; updated 2024: 0.578(86) keV => B = 6.2(9)e-3, arXiv:2404.01564), and f0(1710) has the large radiative production while f0(1500)'s is small. Klempt–Sarantsev (PLB 826, 136906 (2022) 'Singlet-octet-glueball mixing of scalar mesons'; review 'Glueballs in Radiative J/psi Decays' arXiv:2212.06214) instead distribute the glue over f0(1710)/f0(1770)/f0(2020)/f0(2100) with a glueball 'center' ~1965 MeV, width ~370 MeV, summed observed glueball fraction (78±18)% — i.e., even pro-glueball analyses disagree on whether there is ONE glueball state at all, and they split f0(1710) into f0(1710)+f0(1770). Why no confirmation: (i) three-state mixing => no parameter-free prediction; (ii) scalar qqbar background dense and broad; (iii) no G-parity-style forbidden-mode null test exists for 0++ (its discriminants are flavor-symmetric couplings and production systematics, all mixing-sensitive); (iv) contradictory fractions across analyses; (v) historical false alarms (e.g., the narrow tensor fJ(2220) candidate evaporated). This is the explicit contrast the 2026 X(2370) chain claims to beat: a forbidden-channel null (K*Kbar), a measured JPC, and a production rate bracket.

entries.topic: Post-announcement theory support and proposed independent tests
entries.content: (a) Z.-G. Wang, 'Analysis of the X(2370) as a glueball based on rigorous current-field duality', arXiv:2608.03362 (submitted Aug 4, 2026): three-valence-gluon glueball; bosonizes an induced six-quark current via Fierz into three-pseudoscalar operators; obtains model-independent RATIOS of partial widths to three-pseudoscalar final states compatible with BESIII data => supports glueball assignment. (b) 'Investigating the glueball-like particle X(2370) in B meson decays', EPJC 85 (2025) (arXiv:2501.15224): proposes B-decay production as an independent (non-J/psi) arena — relevant to the 'needs confirmation at another facility' caveat (LHCb/Belle II could in principle see it). (c) PACIAE model production study at BESIII and LHC energies, PRD 110, 054046 (2024). (d) The Letter's OWN named future tests (digest Sec.5, VERIFIED locally): omega-omega and phi-phi should be ENHANCED, omega-phi OZI-suppressed, K*(1410)Kbar forbidden by generalized G-parity; precise qqbar mixing fractions require full PWAs including X(2120)/X(2260)/X(2600) interference and threshold effects.

entries.topic: Adversarial map — where each alternative now stands (synthesis)
entries.content: Status as of 2026-08-15: (1) eta/eta' radial excitation — directly contradicted by K*Kbar null (<2 MeV vs 15–200 MeV expected); no published defense found post-Letter. (2) qqbar flavor-singlet — LQCD (Dudek et al. PRD 83, 111502) predicts no light flavor-singlet near 2 GeV; gamma-omega/gamma-phi suppression bounds both light-quark contents; no counter-analysis found. (3) Fully-strange/light tetraquark — was live through Aug 2025 (PRD 112, 034010); Letter argues few-MeV partial widths are un-multiquark-like; no quantitative post-Letter rebuttal found yet (too recent). (4) Baryonium — production too high, no SigmaSigmabar threshold distortion, not flavor-singlet; effectively dead for X(2370) though alive for X(1835). (5) Hybrid — grouped by the Letter with multiquark under 'light-quark content => OZI-allowed ~100 MeV widths expected'; no dedicated X(2370)-hybrid paper surfaced in searches. (6) Glueball-with-ccbar-mixing — the Letter's own position; its keystone (production via ~1°–5° mixing) rests on two 2026 theory papers (2605.01757; Zhang et al. PLB 827 136960) and inverts the 2022 Szczepaniak-group objection. Community verdict: 'glueball-DOMINATED, quite persuasive, no single smoking gun'; open items = mixing fraction quantification, full multi-state PWA, independent non-BESIII confirmation.

findings.topic: MACHINERY 1/3 — what qualifies as a STAKE (corpus's own language)
findings.content: A STAKE is a dated, hashed, pre-registered quantitative wager with (i) a named external adjudicator, (ii) a signed kill clause, (iii) pre-committed response branches (SWP pointers), and (iv) a frozen pipeline behind it. Structural definition is by the stakes-table columns themselves: '# | Stake | Adjudicator | Kill (signed) | SWP' (IX.F). Sec. 0: 'the Stake Letter [stake-letter/2506.α] with stakes table v2 (S1–S7...)... Primary live stake: S1 — Σm_ν ∈ [0.058, 0.11] eV, normal ordering; kill: any robust cosmological determination Σm_ν < 0.058 eV (adjudicators DESI-DR3/Euclid; response pre-committed in Sec. XIII/SWP-1)... The corpus's conduct under every verdict, including its own death, is on the record before the data.' Sec. I.A: 'the price printed on scheduled experiments (Secs. IX, XIII) and the failure conditions signed in advance (Sec. XII).' Sec. I.B (blind/escrow): 'statistics and kill bands are frozen and hashed before computation; unblinding is one step; the pipeline may not be adjusted afterward; post-hoc corrections... demote the affected claim by one grade.'
